title: fix(plugin-audit): a user's own UI-state write writes no ledger row
body:
Fixes #23804
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`writeAudit` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`) now returns before it builds either row when the write is a user's own write to their own per-user UI-state row. The test is the existing `isOwnUiStateWrite` over the closed in-plugin list `PER_USER_UI_STATE_OWNER_FIELD`, today `sys_user_preference` mapped to `user_id`. Until now that test gated only the activity mirror (the #22961 change, PR #22996), so the `sys_audit_log` row was always written. This executes ruling record 6212163130 (letter B, the maintainer's 「同意」), on face 6209004397 and director delta 6211505939.

- **Scope, unchanged predicate.** The acting user (`userId`: the ledger row's `user_id`, the activity row's `actor_id`) must be the owner on every side of the row that names one. No side naming an owner answers `false`. Another actor's write still writes the ledger row and the activity row: an administrator from Setup, a system write with no user, and a write that moves the row to another owner. Nothing about what the test admits was widened.
- **One test, judged once.** The early return sits right after `userId` is resolved and before any read the writer pays for. The activity gate went back to `enable.activities` alone, because the own-write case never reaches it now.
- **Not changed:** `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` / `excludeObjects` / `SKIP_OBJECTS` (the skip is a condition inside `writeAudit`, not an object exclusion); `packages/spec` (`object.zod.ts:259` is untouched); `packages/platform-objects`; objectui. Stored rows stay, and nothing is migrated.
- **Docblock.** The 「ACTIVITY ONLY」 bullet above `PER_USER_UI_STATE_OWNER_FIELD` is now the ledger-and-activity rule and cites ruling record 6212163130. The file-level skip-rule bullet says the same.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/23804-own-ui-state-no-ledger-row.md`, `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit`. Its first paragraph says the ledger no longer records a user's own UI-state writes, and names the consumer this can surprise: an export of `sys_audit_log` to a SIEM or compliance archive.
- The card's Target 2 is met by list membership. Target 3 needs no change (`sys_audit_log_metrics` already reads `config_change`).

## Measured before writing the pins

On a real kernel (`ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + `AuditPlugin`), a real SQLite driver and the shipped `sys_user_preference`, a one-off probe recorded what the engine hands the hook. The probe was not committed.

| write by the owner | `session.userId` | `result` | `previous` | `isOwnUiStateWrite` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| create | owner | full row, `user_id` = owner | none | true |
| update | owner | full row, `user_id` = owner | full row, `user_id` = owner | true |
| delete | owner | `true` (not evidence) | full row, `user_id` = owner | true |

- An owner's update setting `user_id` to null is refused by the engine (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, "User is required and cannot be cleared"), so no write can un-own a row past the test.
- **No other writer records these rows.** The other `sys_audit_log` inserts are `auth-event-audit.ts` (session events), `plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts` (`import` rows about `sys_user`), `service-settings/src/config-change-audit.ts` (`config_change` rows on `sys_setting` / `sys_platform_setting`) and `read-audit.ts` (`read` rows for opted-in objects). None writes a row for a `sys_user_preference` write, and none was changed.
- **Declaration closure unchanged** (`Clause-②: no`). `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` built from this head and from the base's `audit-writers.ts` are byte-identical (`cmp`), and the restore was proven by blob hash equal to HEAD.

## Pins

In two test files, `audit-writers.test.ts` (fake engine) and `audit-writers.own-ui-state.integration.test.ts` (real engine):

- **#22961's fake-engine block**: the three own-write cases (create, update, delete) now assert no `sys_audit_log` row and no `sys_activity` row. The three CONTROL writers (an admin, a system write, a move to another owner) are unchanged and still assert one ledger row and one activity row.
- **New real-engine block** (the kernel above, both tables read at rest by SQL). Each case reads only the rows its own write adds:
  - the owner's own create, update and delete → no ledger row and no activity row; the create and update cases end with an administrator's write to the same row, which must add exactly one ledger row (a live-writer control);
  - an administrator's update of another user's row → one ledger row naming the administrator, plus its activity row;
  - a system write with no user → one ledger row, `user_id` null;
  - the owner moving the row to another user → one ledger row;
  - the same user's update of a `sys_sharing_rule` → one ledger row (the card's Acceptance 1).

## Ablations (committed head `5ff57252e2`; the suite reads `src/` through relative imports, so no `dist/` leg)

Both used `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. The tool verified the anchor count, the blob change and the restore (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty) on disk.

1. **Delete the ledger skip** (`if (isOwnUiStateWrite(ctx.object, userId, before, after)) return;`, anchor 1 → 0): **6 failed / 101 passed**. The failures are exactly the six own-write pins, three fake-engine and three real-engine, for example `expected [ { id: …, …(15) } ] to have a length of +0 but got 1`.
   - A first run of this ablation, before the real-engine cases measured only their own write, failed 9. The extra three (admin, system, move) failed only because their seed is the owner's own create, so with the skip gone the seed added a row. They were decoupled in `5ff57252e2`, and the run above is on that head.
2. **Remove the owner equality** (`return owners.length > 0 && owners.every(…)` → `return owners.length > 0;`): **6 failed / 101 passed**:
   - the fake-engine admin and move CONTROLs;
   - the real-engine admin and move cases;
   - the live-writer control leg of the real-engine own-create and own-update cases, for example `expected [] to deeply equal [ [ 'update', 'u_admin' ] ]` at `audit-writers.test.ts:899` and `:914`.

   The system-write pins and the `sys_sharing_rule` pin stayed green, as predicted: the acting-user check survives that mutation.

Reverse reading at no extra cost: the base's `audit-writers.test.ts`, run against this head's source, fails exactly its three own-write pins (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`).

## Tests and gates (head `03ba0dc800`, after `main` at `a31ff2eb5d` was merged in)

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. The verdict lines are quoted.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test`: **51 files, 840 tests passed** (`VERDICT command-exit 0`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The test layer compiles with 0 errors. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists `src/audit-writers.test.ts` (count 1), so the typecheck reaches the new block.
- `vitest run src/audit-writers.test.ts`: **107 passed** (at `5ff57252e2`, the head the ablations used).
- Dependency closure `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/plugin-audit^...'`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **Derived gates**: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` gave 68 commands for these 3 paths. All 68 ran with the exit code captured before any pipe.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: **68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**.
  - Two gates first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) in the fresh worktree: `pnpm check:i18n` (no built CLI) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (no workspace `dist/`). After their prerequisite builds (turbo replays, 61 of 61 and 74 of 75 cached), each was re-run and exited 0. The `--ran` list carries the re-run codes.
- `pnpm test:repo` was not run locally (CI's `Test Core` runs it): this diff changes no file in that project.
- CI check-runs: pending at the time of writing; the os-dev report on the card cites them.

## Acceptance notes

- **A delegated write counts as the owner's.** For an MCP client acting for the owner (ADR-0090 D10), `session.userId` is the delegator, so that write to the owner's own row is skipped too. The `metadata.performed_by` the ledger would have carried is not written. This is the same predicate the activity half has used since #22961. I did not measure whether any agent writes `sys_user_preference` today.
- **An attributed system write counts as the owner's.** A system-authorized write whose `provenance.attributedUserId` is the owner is judged as the owner's own write (`userId` falls back to it), as on the activity half. The producers of `attributedUserId` are plugin-auth's better-auth adapter and admin flows and plugin-security's auto org-admin grant, and none of them writes `sys_user_preference`.
- **A user's own delete is rarely reachable.** The default permission sets grant `sys_user_preference` with `allowDelete: false` (`plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts:821`), so the own-delete case is mostly a principal with delete rights deleting their own row.
- **This test file got heavier to load.** The new block adds static imports (kernel, ObjectQL, the SQLite driver, the identity objects, `AuditPlugin`) to `audit-writers.test.ts`. Isolated single-file runs on this shared box:
  - base file: 12.53 s total, import 12.19 s;
  - this head: 17.03 s and 17.80 s total, import 16.42 s and 17.21 s;
  - test time: about 120 ms → about 420 ms.

  The base file was already over `FILE_BUDGET_SECONDS` (10 s) in this isolated reading. In the package run, transforms are shared across files (51 files, 65.66 s). The reading is report-only. Carrier: the shard-timings refresh lane, from its CI window.
- **Labels: zero writes.** The dispatch names no label, and `skip-changeset` does not apply (this PR carries a changeset).
- **Card relations.** This PR closes only the card on its first line. #22961 and PR #22996 are cited as the precedent seam and are not addressed here.
